title: The Subjunctive Mood (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Manṣūb)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 15; Ryding Ch. 34)
objectives: Recognise the core subjunctive governing particles (ḥurūf al-naṣb): أنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ, لِـ, and حَتَّى.
Apply the two subjunctive inflectional signs: final fatḥah (-a) and deletion of final nūn (ḥadhf al-nūn).
Parse subordinate purpose clauses and emphatic future negations with لَنْ.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 14: What is the default mood ending on a sound singular imperfect verb like يَكْتُبُ when no governing particle precedes it?

sections.heading: What Triggers the Subjunctive (Al-Naṣb)?
sections.body: An imperfect verb (al-muḍāriʿ) defaults to the indicative mood (marfūʿ). When preceded by a subjunctive particle (ḥarf naṣb), the verb shifts into the subjunctive mood (manṣūb). In Classical Arabic, this commonly expresses purpose ('in order that'), complementation ('that'), or emphatic future negation ('will never').

sections.label: Subjunctive Inflection Rule
sections.summary: After أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ, لِـ, or حَتَّى: sound singular stems replace final ḍammah (-u) with fatḥah (-a), while the five dual/plural forms (al-afʿāl al-khamsah) drop their final nūn.

sections.heading: Indicative vs. Subjunctive Endings
rows: Final nūn dropped; silent alif al-fāriqah added

sections.translation: The student strives in order to understand the lesson.
sections.irab: كَيْ: حَرْفُ نَصْبٍ | يَفْهَمَ: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَنْصُوبٌ بِكَيْ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ
sections.notes: Notice that يَجْتَهِدُ remains indicative (-u) because no particle precedes it, whereas يَفْهَمَ becomes subjunctive (-a) under the governance of كَيْ.

sections.translation: They will never return before sunset.
sections.irab: لَنْ: حَرْفُ نَفْيٍ وَنَصْبٍ | يَرْجِعُوا: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَنْصُوبٌ بِحَذْفِ النُّونِ
sections.notes: Because يَرْجِعُونَ belongs to al-afʿāl al-khamsah, its subjunctive sign is deletion of the final nūn (ḥadhf al-nūn), leaving يَرْجِعُوا.

sections.heading: Do Not Confuse أَنْ with أَنَّ
sections.body: أَنْ (with sukūn on nūn) governs imperfect verbs in the subjunctive. أَنَّ (with shaddah on nūn) belongs to the sisters of إِنَّ and governs nominal clauses.
